statement: For finite D⊆{0,1}^S and c:D→{0,1}^H, a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit outputs c(x) on D and 0^H outside D, with O(S|D|+H|D|) gates.
proof: Build the binary prefix trie of D. Set the root indicator to 1; for each edge, AND the parent indicator with the corresponding input literal. Each leaf indicator is 1 exactly on its word. For each output bit, OR the leaf indicators whose correction has that bit set (use constant 0 if none). On D exactly one leaf is active; outside D none is active. The trie has at most S|D| edges and the output ORs use at most H|D| gates. For D=∅ use constant-zero outputs.

statement: For integers S,H≥0, finite D⊆{0,1}^S, and c:D→{0,1}^H with q=|c(D)|, there is a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit F that equals c on D and 0^H outside D, using at most S|D|+|D|+Hq gates, subject to constant and empty-operation conventions.
proof: Build the prefix trie of D, with one AND gate per edge to produce each leaf indicator; this costs at most S|D| gates. Partition the leaves by their correction vector. For each of the q nonempty groups, OR its leaf indicators, costing |D|-q gates total. For each output bit, OR the group indicators whose correction vector has that bit set, costing at most Hq gates. Exactly one group indicator is active on each x∈D, and none is active outside D. The resulting outputs are therefore c(x) on D and 0^H elsewhere. If D is empty, use constant-zero outputs.

statement: For integers S,H>=0, finite D subseteq {0,1}^S, and c:D->{0,1}^H, write V=c(D). There is a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit F equal to c on D and 0^H outside D with at most S|D|+|D|-|V|+sum_{v in V} wt(v) gates, with constants and wires free. Proof: Build the binary prefix trie of D. For every nonempty prefix create its indicator by ANDing its parent indicator with the corresponding input literal; root indicator is 1. There are at most S|D| such edges/gates. Partition the leaves by their output vector v. OR the indicators in each nonempty group, using |D|-|V| gates total. For output coordinate b, OR the group indicators for vectors v with v_b=1; this uses at most sum_v wt(v) gates total. On each x in D exactly its leaf, hence its output group, is active; outside D no leaf is active. Thus the circuit has the required outputs. Empty D uses constant-zero outputs. This is a general constructive gate-count lemma; it is not claimed to close a recorded P-vs-NP obligation.
proof: As stated in the lemma.

statement: In the fan-in-2 Boolean circuit model where NOT gates are counted and constants and wires are free, for finite D subset {0,1}^S and c:D->{0,1}^H, there is a circuit equal to c on D and 0^H outside D with at most S|D|+|D|-|c(D)|+sum_{v in c(D)}wt(v)+S gates. Proof: create all S negated input literals using S NOT gates. Build the prefix trie of D with at most S|D| AND gates, using the appropriate positive or negative literal on each edge. Group leaves by output vector, costing |D|-|c(D)| OR gates. For each output coordinate, OR the group indicators whose vector has a 1 there, costing at most sum_v wt(v) gates. Exactly the matching leaf group is active on each point in D, and no leaf is active outside D. Empty D uses constant-zero outputs.
proof: Construction and gate accounting as stated; the S shared NOT gates supply all literals used by trie edges.

statement: In the fan-in-2 Boolean circuit model with NOT gates counted and constants and wires free, for integers S,H>=0, a finite set D subseteq {0,1}^S, and c:D->{0,1}^H, there is a circuit F equal to c on D and 0^H outside D with at most S|D|+|D|-|c(D)|+sum_{v in c(D)} wt(v)+S gates. For nonempty D, create all S negated input literals with S NOT gates. Build the prefix trie of D; each of its at most S|D| edges costs one AND gate using the corresponding positive or negative input literal. Group leaf indicators by their output vector, using |D|-|c(D)| OR gates. For each output coordinate b, OR the groups whose vector has a 1 in coordinate b; this uses at most sum_v wt(v) OR gates. On x in D exactly its leaf and output group are active; outside D no leaf is active. For D empty use constant-zero outputs. This is a constructive finite-domain gate bound, not a P-vs-NP result.
proof: The construction and the gate count are given in the statement. For each output coordinate with r contributing groups, OR costs max(r-1,0), which is at most r; summing r over coordinates equals sum_v wt(v). The trie edge count is at most S|D|. The shared NOT gates supply all negated literals, including when S=0, where there are none.

statement: In the fan-in-2 Boolean circuit model with NOT gates counted and constants and wires free, for integers S,H>=0, a finite set D subseteq {0,1}^S, and c:D->{0,1}^H, there is a circuit F equal to c on D and 0^H outside D with at most S|D|+|D|-|c(D)|+sum_{v in c(D)} wt(v)+S gates. For nonempty D, create all S negated input literals with S NOT gates. Build the prefix trie of D; each of its at most S|D| edges costs one AND gate using the corresponding positive or negative input literal. Group leaf indicators by their output vector, using |D|-|c(D)| OR gates. For each output coordinate b, OR the groups whose vector has a 1 in coordinate b; this uses at most sum_v wt(v) OR gates. On x in D exactly its leaf and output group are active; outside D no leaf is active. For D empty use constant-zero outputs. For nonempty D the shared NOT cost is S; for empty D the circuit is constant zero. For each output coordinate with r contributing groups, OR costs max(r-1,0), at most r; summing r over coordinates gives sum_v wt(v). Hence the claimed bound holds for all S,H>=0.

statement: Let S,H>=0, D be a finite subset of {0,1}^S, c:D->{0,1}^H, V=c(D), and B(D)={i in {1,...,S}: there exists x in D with x_i=0}. In the fan-in-2 Boolean circuit model with NOT gates counted and constants and wires free, there is a circuit F:{0,1}^S->{0,1}^H equal to c on D and 0^H outside D with at most S|D|+|D|-|V|+sum_{v in V}wt(v)+|B(D)| gates. Proof: If D is empty, use constant-zero outputs. Otherwise form NOT(x_i) for each i in B(D), using |B(D)| gates. For every coordinate i not in B(D), all points of D have x_i=1, so any trie edge at coordinate i uses the positive literal; for i in B(D), either polarity is available. Build the prefix trie of D, with root indicator 1 and one AND gate for each nonempty-prefix edge, using at most S|D| gates. Group leaf indicators by their c-value; the |V| nonempty groups require |D|-|V| OR gates in total. For output coordinate b, OR the group indicators whose value v has v_b=1; this costs at most the number of such groups, so at most sum_v wt(v) gates over all coordinates. For x in D exactly its leaf and group are active, giving c(x); outside D no leaf is active, giving 0^H. Adding these costs proves the bound. Diagnostic: this is a finite-domain circuit upper bound and claims no P-vs-NP progress.
